title: 20-17, Winner to Be Determined: The Commanders, the Rams and a Gloriously Boring Ref
seoTitle: Commanders vs. Rams Prediction: John Hussey's Crew, Myles Garrett and a 20-17 Call
summary: Commanders vs. Rams: John Hussey's crew by the numbers, no Terry or Burks, Myles Garrett is back, and a 20-17 prediction with no winner attached.
wireTaps: 20-17. You pick the winner, since I clearly can't.
paragraphs: Last week I spent seven straight days warning all of you about Alex Moore. Then the NFL quietly swapped him out, and I spent the first quarter Sunday night yelling the wrong man's name at my television. Shawn Hochuli never heard a word of it. Neither did Alex Moore, who was busy with Patriots-Dolphins. So this week I did my homework twice.
Links up top, like I promised: [who's reffing Sunday](whos-reffing.html), and [Call Your Shot](leaderboard.html), where you can pick the score. Somebody has to, because I'm not going to.
## Ref Watch: A Gloriously Boring Man

Sunday's referee is John Hussey. I checked. Then I checked again. His crews throw 12.2 flags a game, 14th of the 17 refs with enough games to rank and a full flag under the 13.3 league average. He's in a dead heat with Clay Martin for the title of Referee You've Never Heard Of, and Martin only edges him by two hundredths of a flag a game. I have never been this excited about a man's mediocrity.
He's had us exactly once: 2025, Week 5, at the Chargers. Seven flags on us, ten on them, and we won 27-10. Remember that score. It's coming back.

The catch, because there's always a catch: Hussey's crews flag the home team a little more than the visitors, 6.5 a game to 5.7. We're home. Last week the math was wearing burgundy and then the math didn't show up. This week the math is wearing Rams blue, and I've decided not to look directly at it.

People keep asking about my system for watching refs, and by people I mean Google. Last week, folks searched "alex moore crew" and landed on this website, which means the internet was sending people to me for answers while I was screaming at the wrong guy. For the record, here is the system. I go on feel, like a true degenerate fan. If they're flagging us, I get mad. If they're flagging them, the officiating is beautiful. The numbers are mostly a guideline anyway. Alan Eck is the stingiest referee in the league, and he threw ten at us in London.

The whole breakdown is on the [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html): every game Hussey has worked the last two seasons, our flags game by game, and every referee ranked. It updates every Tuesday, so you'll always know who to yell at, even if I don't.
## Who Catches the Ball

Terry is on IR. Treylon Burks is out with his foot. Jason said in the group chat that Burks being out "is a big deal," and he's right, because that's a lot of the people whose job is catching footballs. Antonio Williams has looked good, and I'll keep saying the McLaurin thing with every caveat attached.

If the receiver room gets any thinner, I'd like the front office to know I'm available. I never played a down of college football, which means I still have all four years of NCAA eligibility. Somebody just has to coach me up. My forty time is best measured in ounces.

Myles Garrett is back for the Rams. My official reaction in the group chat can't be printed on a family website, but it started with one swear and ended with "Garrett coming back." Jason hopes he's on a snap count. So do I. So does every tackle we have.
## The Group Chat's Pregame Takes

I asked the boys for real talk: do we win Sunday? Jason went first. "Ehh; I am not confident." He thinks the West Coast to East Coast trip is real, and that Jayden is always capable, but "we're so beat up, we're not really good, I'm not getting excited. I don't think we get slaughtered, but I'm assuming a loss." That's the most Jason sentence ever typed. Hope, a travel theory, a diagnosis, and then a loss anyway.

Chris's pregame take, in full: does he need a MacBook Pro, or is a MacBook Air okay? That was it. That was the whole take. I told him the Air is one million percent fine, which is the most confident I've been about anything this week.
## My Number: 20-17

Vegas has the Rams by four and a half. On paper, despite their 4-4 record, we should get wrecked. So in the group chat I said this, and I'm putting it in writing: no turnovers, this game is 20-17. I can't say who it'll be, but 20-17. I stand by it. Both halves of it.

A score with no winner is either the safest prediction in sports history or a cry for help, and I'm not ruling out either one. Consider it a non-binding estimate. My last pick was 27-13 and the final was 27-10, which was close enough to put me first on the [leaderboard](leaderboard.html) with a 1-2 record. First place with a losing record. This is the NFC East of leaderboards.
You don't get to be as vague as me. [Call your shot](leaderboard.html), put a name on it, and pick a winner. Somebody in this household should.

We got our flu and COVID shots this week, so this one is a couch game for sure. Two freshly vaccinated adults, one remote, 1 p.m. kickoff on FOX. Honestly, a home game at a normal hour on my own couch is my favorite way to watch football now. I'm 45. I have earned the couch.

Here's the hope part, because there's always a hope part. The last time John Hussey had us, we won 27-10. Last Sunday, with a totally different ref, we won 27-10. If it's 20-17, I was right. If it's 27-10 again, I'm calling it a pattern. Hail.
